introduction.p: Fill in the variables A\text{,} B\text{,} and C in Ax + By = C with the numbers 10, 11 and 14\text{.} You may only use each number once in each part.

statement.p: For the steepest possible slope, A must be , B must be , and C must be .

solution.p: Lets put Ax + By = C into slope-intercept form. Then, the equation becomes y = \frac{-A}{B}x + \frac{C}{B}\text{.} To make the steepest slope possible, we must maximize the fraction \frac{A}{B}\text{.} The possibilities are \frac{10}{11}\text{,} \frac{10}{14}\text{,} \frac{11}{10}\text{,} \frac{11}{14}\text{,} \frac{14}{10}\text{,} and \frac{14}{11}\text{.} The biggest of these is \frac{14}{10}\text{.} Thus, A must equal 14, B must equal 10, and C must equal 11.

statement.p: For the shallowest possible slope, A must be , B must be , and C must be .

solution.p: To make the shallowest slope possible, we must minimize the fraction \frac{A}{B}\text{.} The smallest of the possible fractions is \frac{10}{14}\text{.} Thus, A must equal 10, B must equal 14, and C must equal 11.
